result.question: I'm worried the paper insulation in Transformer 1 at MAIN may be involved. Pull co and co2 for every sample in the available window and work out the CO2/CO ratio for each sample. Flag any sample with a ratio below 3, which suggests paper involved in a fault, or above 10, which suggests general cellulose ageing. Also give me the min, max and mean of co and co2 over the window. Tell me whether the ratio is trending up or down across the samples. If co2 is missing for a sample, skip the ratio for that sample and say so. If co2 has no data at all, report the co trend alongside oxygen instead and say that the ratio test couldn't be done.
result.answer:
I have everything needed—no further tool calls required. Here's the analysis.

## Transformer 1 (MAIN) — CO₂/CO ratio analysis

**Window:** 2024-01-15 → 2024-01-19, 5 daily samples. Both `co` and `co2` were present and non-null for every sample, so no ratios had to be skipped.

### Per-sample ratios

| Timestamp | CO (ppm) | CO₂ (ppm) | CO₂/CO | Flag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15 | 32 | 1344 | 42.00 | ⚠ >10 — general cellulose ageing |
| 2024-01-16 | 30 | 1300 | 43.33 | ⚠ >10 — general cellulose ageing |
| 2024-01-17 | 35 | 1350 | 38.57 | ⚠ >10 — general cellulose ageing |
| 2024-01-18 | 33 | 1325 | 40.15 | ⚠ >10 — general cellulose ageing |
| 2024-01-19 | 32 | 1340 | 41.88 | ⚠ >10 — general cellulose ageing |

- **Below 3 (paper involved in an active fault):** none.
- **Above 10 (general cellulose ageing):** all 5 samples.

### Window statistics

| Gas | Min | Max | Mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| CO | 30 | 35 | 32.4 |
| CO₂ | 1300 | 1350 | 1331.8 |

### Ratio trend
The ratio is **slightly trending down** (least-squares slope ≈ −0.34 per day; 42.0 on day 1 → 41.9 on day 5, low of 38.6 on 01-17), but the movement is small and oscillatory rather than a clean directional drift — over a 5-day window it's effectively flat in the 38–43 band.

### Interpretation
The consistently high ratio (~40) points to slow, thermal ageing of the cellulose insulation rather than paper being caught up in an active fault — the ratio is nowhere near the <3 region that would indicate the latter. CO and CO₂ absolute levels are also stable day-to-day (CO stddev ≈ 1.6 ppm, CO₂ ≈ 18 ppm), which doesn't suggest an accelerating process. If you want to firm this up, the next useful steps would be running the hydrocarbon gases through the Rogers-ratio interpretation (`interpret_dga`) to check for an accompanying thermal fault, and checking furan/water content trends for degree-of-polymerisation context.
